summary.text: A 65-year-old woman with recurrent high grade endometrial carcinoma with serous and endometrioid features. Initial surgery showed disease limited to the uterus and endocervical canal, and CT later showed inguinal adenopathy consistent with stage IV disease; paclitaxel and carboplatin gave a complete response by imaging.

HER2 immunohistochemical stain was negative (0+) while NGS showed a pathogenic HER2 p.G776V mutation; ER and PR were patchy, p53 overexpressed and mismatch repair proteins retained. Eighteen months later imaging showed metastatic disease; checkpoint inhibitor-based therapy on a trial gave a partial response with progression after eight months, then paclitaxel and carboplatin were re-administered and two additional lines of cytotoxic chemotherapy including bevacizumab ended in progression.

She then began T-DXd, with CA-125 decreasing from 177 to 23 within six weeks and decreasing size of metastatic lesions; over 12 additional months imaging showed stable low-volume disease with CA-125 in the normal range. After cycle 17 T-DXd was held for thrombocytopenia and hyperbilirubinemia and a bone marrow biopsy revealed myelodysplastic syndrome.

CT five months later showed progression; she began single agent trastuzumab and remains on it with stable disease at five months. The total treatment duration from diagnosis of metastatic disease is four years and five months.

summary.text: A 76-year-old woman with recurrent low grade serous ovarian carcinoma and unresectable disease on diagnostic laparoscopy received paclitaxel and carboplatin then gemcitabine and carboplatin with a partial response, then letrozole with stable disease for one year.

Radical cytoreductive surgery completely resected peritoneal disease leaving a residual 2 cm cecal mass; colonoscopy later confirmed multifocal low grade serous carcinoma in the colon. Letrozole was resumed for 12 months until CA-125 rose and repeat colonoscopy showed possible progression; oral cyclophosphamide and bevacizumab were followed by progression after 6 months.

NGS showed a large HER2 deletion including exon 16 while HER2 immunohistochemistry on a small metastatic deposit was negative (IHC 0). Single agent trastuzumab gave stable disease for over two years; a MAPK-pathway trial for eight months ended in progression.

She began T-DXd with a partial response and improving PET avidity, remains on it after over two years, and after cycle 42 developed neutropenia requiring the dose frequency to decrease from every three to every four weeks.

summary.text: A 52-year-old woman with recurrent cervical mesonephric adenocarcinoma; her initial diagnosis was a high-grade adenocarcinoma of uterine versus cervical origin, presumptive stage IIB. She had preoperative pelvic radiation for one month followed by robotic-assisted total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, left parametrium removal and pelvic lymph node dissection; pelvic nodes were negative and she was cancer free postoperatively.

She received three cycles of adjuvant paclitaxel and carboplatin and vaginal brachytherapy before being lost to follow up. Three years later she presented with abdominal pain and CT showing carcinomatosis, with a biopsy consistent with recurrent cervical mesonephric adenocarcinoma.

Eight cycles of paclitaxel, carboplatin, bevacizumab and pembrolizumab gave a partial response; maintenance bevacizumab and pembrolizumab for a year ended with progression on surveillance CT. NGS revealed an activating HER2 p.I767M mutation and HER2 immunohistochemical staining was not performed.
T-DXd gave a partial response on imaging about six weeks later, maintained until progression 15 months after starting; gastrointestinal toxicity and neutropenia required dose reductions.
